text.text_excerpt: Casual, relaxed, intimate, and delicious. Very attentive service, and the owner is usually on site making sure his patrons are happy and well-fed. Italian opera played in the dimly lit dining room. We shared the spinach/artichoke bruschetta app, which was basically just spinach/artichoke dip on slices of toasted baguette -- simple but tasty. The salads were amazing -- try the caesar, which has a homemade dressing with a little spice/bite to it, and/or the salad with almonds and bleu cheese. Lots of tasty looking pizzas on the menu as well -- we had the quattro fromaggio with mushrooms on it and some nice zesty marinara on the side, which was on the better side of average. My husband and I visited on a Saturday night. Nice crowd, and there were still a couple of empty tables outside, so we stayed outside to enjoy one of our brief, beautiful Spring evenings. My husband asked for the wine list and our waitress read from her cheat sheet what wines they had that evening. He was a little surprised, but picked out a nice pinot noir for our dinner. We started the meal with the mixed green salad. We've had it before and I was looking forward to the candied almonds and Gorgonzola cheese over the mixed greens. I too visited Figaro's because of the Groupon I purchased. C was in town and it was Friday, so we decided to go out for dinner. C invited a friend and friend's girlfriend and I made a reservation for four. About half an hour before our reservation, we thought that our friends wouldn't make it, so we showed up and told the hostess that it was just going to be the two of us. Not long after we sat down and ordered (and I had a glass of some nice Pinot Grigio in front of me), C got a call from friend saying that they could come then if still welcome.
